critique.evidence: The screen strongly connects evaluation to fraud operations through constrained-FPR recall, calibration, alert load, latency, confusion counts, fraud value caught, and good value blocked. Its provenance ablation also links defense components to measured PR-AUC. However, the intent-integrity case is not fully proven: removing Semantic shows only a 0.010 PR-AUC decrease, while fresh-row recall remains 100% for every configuration, so the key semantic/intent layer appears operationally unnecessary. The screen also lacks explicit Mastercard/payment-network grounding and does not identify the transaction corpus, value basis, or attack classes behind the results.
critique.fix: Add an intent-manipulation benchmark broken down by attack class and payment scenario, showing full-defense versus no-semantic/no-provenance effects at the same false-positive cap. Include transaction count, test-set provenance, decision threshold, monetary basis, and a Mastercard-relevant outcome such as prevented fraud value versus legitimate payment value declined.
